text:
Senator John Curtis addresses disaster response and child online safety legislation
P. D. Arnold
Senator John Curtis, who represents Utah’s 3rd district in the U.S. Congress, posted a series of messages on August 5, 2026, addressing recent legislative efforts and concerns about extreme weather and online safety for children.
In a post from August 5, 2026, Curtis highlighted the impact of severe weather events: "Extreme weather is taking a devastating toll on communities across the country. In Utah, we've seen firsthand the impacts of catastrophic wildfires and flooding. Joined my Senate colleagues and experts to discuss how we can better protect communities from natural disasters," he wrote.
Later that day, Curtis addressed challenges faced by families in the digital age: "As a parent of parents, I've seen firsthand how overwhelming it is to raise children in our social media-driven world. Today I was proud to help advance meaningful legislation to give families the tools and transparency they need to keep their kids safer online."
He followed up with another message outlining specific legislative measures: "These bills—including our CHATBOT Act and Kids Online Safety Act—will empower parents and protect children without stifling innovation."
Curtis has served as Utah’s representative since 2017 after succeeding Jason Chaffetz. He was born in Salt Lake City in 1960 and resides in Provo. Curtis graduated from Brigham Young University with a Bachelor of Science degree in 1985.
